title: Flatness at points is upward and downward stable along cartesian change of base, with the flat-locus base-change corollary
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For a cartesian square of schemes X' -> X over S' -> S and a quasi-coherent module F flat over S at x versus its pullback flat over S' at x', the lemma proves both transport directions: (1) flatness of F at x descends to flatness of (g')^*F at x'; (2) if g is flat at s', flatness of (g')^*F at x' reflects back to flatness of F at x; and the corollary: with g flat and f, F locally of finite presentation, the openness-theorem flat locus commutes with arbitrary base change. The retained proof is complete: at the local-ring square, O_{X',x'} is a localization of O_{X,x} (x)_{O_{S,s}} O_{S',s'} and ((g')^*F)_{x'} = F_x (x) O_{X',x'}, so both statements are the ring-theoretic base-change flatness up-down lemma (Algebra, lemma base-change-flat-up-down) applied verbatim; the finite-presentation corollary reads off the theorem's definition of the flat locus. Retained author proof at lines 4494-4509.
